    Grow a farm. Herd size and methane emissions are coupled by default — decoupling them takes deliberate investment.

    Healthy farm

    Methane is a far more potent greenhouse gas than CO2 over the short term — roughly 80x stronger over 20 years — which makes industrial agriculture's methane output an outsized lever for near-term warming, even though it fades from the atmosphere faster than CO2 does.

      i

      Pressure scales with your total accumulated methane (not your current herd size or ratio), so it never resets — even emissions from many rounds ago keep dragging down income permanently. It caps at 80% income loss, so a runaway strategy gets much worse but never fully bankrupts you.

      Score: 300

      i

      Score is not just your funds — it's funds minus your total accumulated methane multiplied by a fixed penalty weight. A big bank balance built on high, unchecked emissions can score lower than a smaller, cleaner farm.

      i

      Feed Additives, Herd Caps, and Capture Systems all reduce the same underlying emissions ratio, and their effects stack additively — investing in several compounds rather than duplicating effort. The ratio has a floor, though: past a certain point, further investment stops helping.

      Alternative protein pivot

      i

      This is a separate lever from Feed/Caps/Capture — it changes what fraction of output is plant-based instead of making animal production more efficient, and cuts methane per unit much further. The tradeoff: plant-based output earns slightly less income per unit, and it can only replace up to 60% of production.

          Farm succession

          i

          A certified farm can be handed to the next generation. The farm restarts from scratch, and the outgoing farm earns legacy points (a bonus if it raised a poultry flock) that buy permanent perks for every generation to come, such as keeping the poultry flock available from round 1.

          Poultry flock (unlocked by certification)

          i

          A second herd type with its own, much lower emissions curve, its own levers and housing upkeep. Your certified farm earned the right to diversify. Real poultry emissions are mostly manure nitrous oxide and ammonia rather than enteric methane, so the game shows a single methane-equivalent number.

          Satellite farm

          i

          A smaller, older second farm in your regional network, with its own emissions ratio and its own barn retrofits. The network effect: once your main farm is decoupled past 40%, the know-how and equipment you paid for at home spill over and cut the satellite's emissions too, up to half. Its output still counts toward your methane total and any regional cap.
